figures.caption: Table 5: Representative regex trigger patterns for the deterministic 8-category classifier. The full pattern set (∼30 sub-rules) is shipped with the harness; each category line above gives a one-line digest of the patterns it dispatches against.

Figure 1: Repair by degeneration. Here, the racecar denotes an optimized GPU kernel and the bicycle a correct-but-slow fallback; a useful repair preserves optimization structure, but LLMs often simplify candidates into slower correct programs.

Figure 4: (Left) Per-model degeneration evidence on the corpus’s eventually-passing tasks: median speedup of iter-1 passes vs. iter-N (N>1) passes, and the degeneration rate (share of iter-N passes whose speedup falls below the reference baseline, i.e. <1.0×). (Right) Per-model pass@5 vs. performance-gate p. Dashed line marks the default p=0.7.

Table 6: Per-model stagnation breakdown on failing tasks under the default protocol. nfail is the number of tasks that never passed within K = 5 iterations. overall is the fraction of those tasks where any of the four stagnation signals fired (remaining tasks reach max_iterations without firing a signal); the four signal columns sum to overall by construction.
Figure 5: Feedback richness A3 (left) and conversation-history depth A4 (right). Per-model pass@k trajectories; star marks each model’s best setting, dashed grey line marks the default.
Figure 2: Corpus coverage across workload size (lines of code, log scale, x), various domains (y), and 5 curation-time failure-modes (color, collapsed from the 8-category per-iteration taxonomy).

Table 13: Per-fixer fix_rate per 5-bucket curation-time error category (§3.5, Section E). Each cell is the fraction of broken-starts in that bucket that the fixer eventually solved at any iteration under correctness-only scoring (p=0). timeout is sparse (n=2) and not interpretable. Gemma-4-31B-it’s denominators are smaller (n=78/34/41/13/2 for compile/logic/perf-broken/mem-crash/timeout) because its manifest covers 168 of 200 v2 tasks; rates are reported within available coverage.
Table 14: Corpus instances by kernel family (11 families, two tiers).
Table 4: Eight-category error taxonomy with five-bucket collapse.

Table 3: Per-fixer pass@k stratified by difficulty tier at the default protocol (p=0.7). Tiers are computed over the six fixers (excluding MiniMax-M2.7); MiniMax row is reported on the same tier partition for comparability. L5 tasks are unsolved by every fixer in the tier-induction set, so all fixers register 0% on this slice by construction; L5 thus measures residual solvability beyond the tier-induction set, which is empirically zero on this corpus. MiniMax’s L1 row (50%) is therefore not anomalous: L1 membership is defined relative to the six-model tier-induction set, not MiniMax.

Figure 3: Iterative vs. repeated debugging pipelines (axis A2). The iterative pipeline appends feedback after each failed attempt and exits early on success; the repeated pipeline resets to the initial prompt each attempt. Both feed identical outputs to the same pass@k aggregator.
